aeMode.title: Exposure mode
aeMode.hint: Automatic follows the light within the limits below; manual holds what you set.
aeMode.help: In automatic mode the exposure and gains below are limits auto-exposure works inside. In manual they are the values themselves, and only what is set is held: an exposure or gain left empty goes on following the light. The reaction settings wait for automatic mode.

exposure.title: Longest exposure
exposure.hint: Empty is automatic. The longer you allow, the lower the frame rate can fall in the dark: 100 ms is at most 10 frames a second.
exposure.help: In automatic mode this is the longest auto-exposure may use. In manual it is the exposure itself, still bounded by the frame period. Fractional: 0.5 is half a millisecond.

aGain.title: Highest analog gain
aGain.hint: 1x adds no gain; 2x doubles the signal and its noise. Empty is automatic.
aGain.help: In automatic mode this is the highest auto-exposure may use; in manual it is the gain itself. Tenths are fine: 1.5 is one and a half times.

dGain.title: Highest sensor digital gain
dGain.hint: Empty is automatic: 1x while slow shutter is on, and the sensor's own limit with it off, which can be over 100x. In manual mode it does nothing.
dGain.help: Unlike the other two gains this one is a ceiling and never a value. These sensors carry a single combined gain register, so there is no separate digital gain to hold at a figure; measured, a manual setting here leaves the picture and the raw data untouched. Use the analog gain when the exposure mode is manual.

ispGain.title: Highest ISP gain
ispGain.hint: Applied after the raw data is read, so it brightens the picture and not a RAW snapshot. Empty is automatic.
ispGain.help: In automatic mode this is the highest auto-exposure may use; in manual it is the gain itself.

aeStrategy.title: Metering priority
aeStrategy.hint: Which end of the picture keeps its detail when both cannot, such as a lit number plate at night.
aeStrategy.help: Protect highlights holds the bright end down, for a scene whose subject is the brightest thing in it; protect shadows favours the dark end. The camera's choice restores what the image pipeline picked on its own.

aeSpeed.title: Reaction speed
aeSpeed.hint: A step with no unit, 1 to 255: higher chases a change in light sooner and can visibly pump. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeSpeed.help: Empty, or 0, keeps whatever the camera's image profile asked for, which is what most cameras should run. Raise it for a doorway or a gateway where the light changes as something passes; lower it for a scene with moving highlights, where a fast reaction shows up as the whole picture breathing.

aeTolerance.title: Tolerance
aeTolerance.hint: How far brightness may drift from its target, in levels out of 255, before exposure moves. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeTolerance.help: Empty, or 0, keeps the image profile's value. Raising it stops small changes in the scene from moving the picture; raise it far enough and the camera stops correcting for real changes too.

aeBlackDelay.title: Darkening delay
aeBlackDelay.hint: Frames to wait before reacting to the picture getting darker. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeBlackDelay.help: Empty, or 0, keeps the image profile's value. Useful where something briefly blocks the view — a lorry, a bird, a hand over the lens — and you would rather the camera sat still than opened up and closed again.

aeWhiteDelay.title: Brightening delay
aeWhiteDelay.hint: Frames to wait before reacting to the picture getting brighter. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeWhiteDelay.help: Empty, or 0, keeps the image profile's value. The counterpart to the darkening delay, for a scene where headlights or a torch sweep through and the picture should not dive after them.

slowShutter.title: Slow shutter
slowShutter.hint: In the dark, lets one exposure last longer than a frame: a brighter, less noisy picture at a lower frame rate, and more blur on anything moving.
slowShutter.help: At 25 fps, low goes down to 12.5 fps, medium to 10 and high to 7.5. A longest exposure set below takes its place. Off keeps the frame rate and brightens with gain alone. It also sets the gain limits used while those are empty: 32x analog, 1x sensor digital and 4x ISP with slow shutter on, the sensor's own limits with it off.

dehaze.title: Dehaze strength
dehaze.hint: Lifts contrast through haze and fog. 0 turns it off; -1 lets the camera's image profile vary it with the light.
dehaze.help: It is a contrast stretch: helpful in haze, and a night scene it was not asked for loses shadow detail to it. -1 hands the block to the IQ profile instead, which is the only way its [dynamic_dehaze] curve can run — any strength at all forces the manual mode the curve is ignored in. The default is unchanged at 125, so no camera moves without being told to.

externalTuner.title: Hand the picture to a tuning tool
externalTuner.hint: Stops the camera re-applying its own image settings, so a tool like PQTools can change them. For a tuning session only.
externalTuner.help: The profile's ISO ladders are pushed every ten seconds and automatic tuning moves contrast and dehaze every couple of seconds, so a value written from outside is overwritten before anyone can look at it. While this is on, none of those run and a day/night change does not re-read the profile. Turn it off and the camera takes the picture back on the next tick — nothing is saved, so read the result out with GET /api/v1/isp/profile.ini before you do.

meterRect.title: Metering area
meterRect.hint: The part of the picture exposure is judged on. Draw one around a subject much brighter or darker than the rest; empty uses the whole picture.
meterRect.help: Use it when the subject is much brighter or darker than its surroundings — a lit number plate clips at the exposure the rest of a night scene needs. The camera's metering window is at least 256x120, so a smaller rectangle is grown around its own centre. Written as XxYxWxH.
